hints: Focus on what first ionisation energy really measures, removal of an electron from a separate gaseous atom, not from a molecule.
Compare sulfur ($Z=16$) and chlorine ($Z=17$) in Period 3, both lose a 3p electron with very similar inner shielding.
Ask yourself which change, more protons or similar shielding, increases the pull on that outer electron, and ignore any talk of $\text{Cl-Cl}$ or $\text{S-S}$ bonds.
walkthrough:
**Recall what first ionisation energy depends on**

Think of it as how tightly the nucleus holds the outer electron. It is a property of single gaseous atoms.

$$\text{X(g)} \rightarrow \text{X}^{+}\text{(g)} + e^{-}$$
Three things matter: nuclear charge, shielding, and atomic radius.

**Compare S and Cl across Period 3**

Sulfur is $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^4$ and chlorine is $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5$. They are neighbours in the same period.

So shielding by inner shells is almost identical, but chlorine has one extra proton ($17$ vs $16$).

**Decide each statement**

Statement 1 is true. Greater nuclear charge with similar shielding gives greater effective nuclear charge, so the 3p electron is held more tightly.

Statement 2 is false. Shielding does not increase significantly across a period. Statement 3 is false because ionisation energy says nothing about covalent bond strength in $\text{Cl}_2$ or $\text{S}_8$.

**Choose the combination**

Only statement 1 contributes. That corresponds to 1 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 are all true. Statements 2 and 3 are not true, so this cannot be chosen.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 are both true. While 1 is correct, shielding is essentially the same for S and Cl in Period 3, so 2 is false.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 are true. Shielding is not greater for chlorine, and molecular bond strength has no effect on atomic first ionisation energy.
options.D: Correct. Only 1 is true. Chlorine has greater nuclear charge ($17$ protons vs $16$) with similar shielding, so effective nuclear charge is higher and the 3p electron is harder to remove.
